messages:
maya: Heads up — ran a perf job on prod-like load and hit a KV-cache-driven OOM while continuous batching was enabled. Observed after the recent kernel-selector change.

sam: ugh. which change exactly?

maya: kernel-selector now prefers the new fused-attn kernel for short sequences; that causes slightly higher KV peak due to larger per-shard state for the cache allocator. Noticed memory spikes when batches included many long-prefix requests.

devin: can you paste the run log?

maya: sure, here's the offending snippet we got from the node that OOM'd:

```
[2026-02-14T18:34:12Z] runtime: assembling batch id=9832 size=18 total_tokens=672 kv_bytes=1.9G
[2026-02-14T18:34:13Z] cuda: alloc failed: cuMemAlloc 2048M -> CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED
[2026-02-14T18:34:13Z] runtime: batch 9832 -> eviction attempt failed (no evictable frames) -> soft-oom
```

maya: That batch had 6 requests with very large prefixes (1k tokens). The batch assembler had a token-budget target of 700 tokens but didn't account for KV footprint per-token for this kernel.

sam: so token budget isn't proportional to KV bytes for that kernel. we need a kernel-specific kv multiplier.

frank: agree — we should add a kernel->kv-per-token lookup used during batch formation. Current heuristic uses token_count * avg_kv_bytes_per_token (global) which is wrong after the kernel switch.

devin: propose two quick mitigations: 1) clamp max batch token budget per-queue for kernels flagged as KV-heavy; 2) reserve a KV-headroom (%) per GPU that batch assembler never consumes. Which to prioritize?

maya: both. start with KV-headroom reserve to avoid crashes. I suggest reserve = max(512MB, 10% of allocatable-GPU-memory) to be safe.

sam: sounds good. Also we should add a pre-admission check that computes estimated_kv_bytes_for_batch and rejects/adapts the batch if (estimated_kv + current_kv_used) > allocatable - reserve.

frank: that pre-admission code can reuse existing admissions API. Small pseudo:

```
est_kv = sum(req.tokens * kernel_kv_multiplier[kernel_id] for req in batch)
if current_kv + est_kv > gpu_limit - kv_reserve:
    if batch.size > 1: trim_batch_by_smallest_prefix()
    else: reject_with_backoff()
```

maya: I ran a quick microbenchmark to estimate multipliers. For fused-attn short seqs it was ~3.2 bytes/token, for the old kernel ~1.1 bytes/token (on A100 80GB). I'll attach the numbers after lunch.

sam: nice — we'll need these numbers in a table for CVs and to store in the kernel profile cache. Also ensure the kernel selector returns the kernel_id to the batcher so we can pick the right multiplier.

devin: on the admission policy: prefer trimming long-prefix requests first (LIFO?) to avoid head-of-conversation regressions. Maybe a weight: prefix_tokens * user_priority -> score. Lower score get trimmed.

frank: +1. Also add an adaptive backoff that increases the per-request token-limit when repeated trims happen, to avoid starvation.

maya: ops-bot recorded the node allocation and current KV metrics for the run:

ops-bot: node/gpu-24: allocatable=75.3GB, current_kv=42.1GB, reserve=8.0GB (10%), available_for_batches=25.2GB

maya: With that available_for_batches, the batch with est_kv=18.9GB pushed us over when combined with the runtime overhead of the fused kernel.

sam: timeline: I'll put a short PR for kv_reserve + admission check today (low risk). frank can follow with kernel_kv multipliers and profile cache. devin you ok to land trimming policy?

devin: yep I'll draft the trimming algo and tests. plan: unit tests for estimator, integration test simulating mixed prefixes (fast).

frank: for observability we should emit: estimated_kv, kernel_id, kv_reserve_at_decision, trim_reason per admission decision. That will make postmortem queries easier.

maya: agreed. also add a metric for "kv_reserve_hits" to track how often reserve prevents an OOM.

sam: one more thought — could we leverage prefix caching TTL to reduce KV peaks? e.g., temporarily compress cold KV frames to 4-bit quantized storage during pressure? heavier work but long-term win.

frank: interesting but complex. note for roadmap. short-term fixes first.

maya: I'll attach the microbenchmark CSV and a short repro script in the thread's followups. For now we can triage as P1 perf-regression since it causes OOMs.

devin: ack. I'll add test harness that simulates fused-attn kernel kv-per-token and run overnight with batcher changes.

sam: thanks all. ping me if you need GPUs for testing — I'll grab a few lower-priority nodes. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks — will follow up with numbers. :rocket:
